cases.sentence: Элен понимала, что дело было очень просто и легко с ___ зрения, но что ее руководители делали затруднения только потому, что они опасались, каким образом светская власть посмотрит на это дело.
cases.explain: «духовной точки» — after the preposition «с», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Elèn understood that the question was very simple and easy from the ecclesiastical point of view, and that her directors were making difficulties only because they were apprehensive as to how the matter would be regarded by the secular authorities.

cases.sentence: Она вызвала ревность старика-вельможи и сказала ему то же, что̀ ___, т. е. поставила вопрос так, что единственное средство получить права на нее состояло в том, чтобы жениться на ней.
cases.explain: «первому искателю» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: So she decided that it was necessary to prepare the opinion of society. She provoked the jealousy of the elderly magnate and told him what she had told her other suitor; that is, she put the matter so that the only way for him to obtain a right over her was to marry her. The elderly magnate was at first as much taken aback by this suggestion of marriage with a woman whose husband was alive, as the younger man had been, but Elèn’s imperturbable conviction that it was as simple and natural as marrying a maiden had its effect on him too. Had Elèn herself shown the least sign of hesitation, shame, or secrecy, her cause would certainly have been lost; but not only did she show no signs of secrecy or shame, on the contrary, with good-natured naivete she told her intimate friends (and these were all Petersburg) that both the prince and the magnate had proposed to her and that she loved both and was afraid of grieving either.

cases.sentence: Встретив Элен на бале, Марья Дмитриевна остановила ее по середине залы, и при ___ своим грубым голосом сказала ей:
cases.explain: «общем молчании» — after the preposition «при», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Only Márya Dmítrievna Akhrosímova, who had come to Petersburg that summer to see one of her sons, allowed herself plainly to express an opinion contrary to the general one. Meeting Elèn at a ball she stopped her in the middle of the room and, amid general silence, said in her gruff voice: “So wives of living men have started marrying again! Perhaps you think you have invented a novelty? You have been forestalled, my dear! It was thought of long ago. It is done in all the brothels,” and with these words Márya Dmítrievna, turning up her wide sleeves with her usual threatening gesture and glancing sternly round, moved across the room.

cases.sentence: Ну так, ___ мое, ты знаешь, что сердце отца твоего радуется тому, что ты...
cases.explain: «милое дитя» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Prince Vasíli, who of late very often forgot what he had said and repeated one and the same thing a hundred times, remarked to his daughter whenever he chanced to see her: “Hélène, I have a word to say to you,” and he would lead her aside, drawing her hand downward. “I have heard of certain projects concerning … you know. Well my dear child, you know how your father’s heart rejoices to know that you … You have suffered so much. … But, my dear child, consult only your own heart. That is all I have to say,” and concealing his unvarying emotion he would press his cheek against his daughter’s and move away.

cases.sentence: (Вы знаете, ведь тут замешано родство.) А если выйти за ___, то вы составите счастие последних дней его, и потом... принцу уже не будет унизительно жениться на вдове вельможи.
cases.explain: «старого графа» — after the preposition «за», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: (You know there is some kind of connection.) But if you marry the old count you will make his last days happy, and as widow of the Grand … the prince would no longer be making a mésalliance by marrying you,” and Bilíbin smoothed out his forehead. “That’s a true friend!” said Elèn beaming, and again touching Bilíbin’s sleeve. “But I love them, you know, and don’t want to distress either of them. I would give my life for the happiness of them both.”

cases.sentence: — сказал он, вследствие твердости своей репутации не боясь уронить себя таким ___.
cases.explain: «наивным вопросом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “But tell me, how will your husband look at the matter?” Bilíbin asked, his reputation being so well established that he did not fear to ask so naive a question. “Will he agree?”

cases.explain: «старая княгиня» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “But it says plainly: ‘Whosoever shall marry her that is divorced …’ ” said the old princess.

cases.sentence: В моем положении есть обязанности, — заговорила Элен, переводя разговор на французский с ___, на котором ей всегда казалась какая-то неясность в ее деле.
cases.explain: «русского языка» — after the preposition «с», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Ah, Maman, ne dites pas de bêtises. Vous ne comprenez rien. Dans ma position j’ai des devoirs,”96 said Elèn changing from Russian, in which language she always felt that her case did not sound quite clear, into French which suited it better.

cases.sentence: — Ah, maman, comment est-ce que vous ne comprenez pas que le Saint Père, qui a le droit de donner des dispenses...[757] Ах, маменька, как вы не понимаете, что ___, имеющий власть отпущений...
cases.explain: «святой отец» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Oh, Mamma, how is it you don’t understand that the Holy Father, who has the right to grant dispensations …”

cases.sentence: — Графиня, есть милосердие для всякого греха, — сказал входя молодой, белокурый человек с ___ и носом.
cases.explain: «длинным лицом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Non, dites-lui que je ne veux pas le voir, que je suis furieuse contre lui, parce qu’il m’a manqué parole.”97 “Comtesse, à tout péché miséricorde,”98 said a fair-haired young man with a long face and nose, as he entered the room.

cases.explain: «Старая княгиня» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The old princess rose respectfully and curtsied. The young man who had entered took no notice of her. The princess nodded to her daughter and sidled out of the room.

cases.sentence: «Нет, она права», думала ___, все убеждения которой разрушились пред появлением его высочества.
cases.explain: «старая княгиня» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Yes, she is right,” thought the old princess, all her convictions dissipated by the appearance of His Highness. “She is right, but how is it that we in our irrecoverable youth did not know it? Yet it is so simple,” she thought as she got into her carriage.
